title: TikTok Will Now Scan for AI Clones of Your Face
hook: Worried an AI has faked a video of your face on TikTok? A new opt-in tool verifies who you are, then scans the app for AI content wearing your likeness — and lets you report it.
key_points: TikTok is testing an opt-in tool that scans the app for AI-generated content using a creator's face.
To enable it, creators verify their identity via Jumio: a live selfie plus an ID check.
TikTok says it doesn't keep the ID document; facial data is used only to match likeness matches.
Matches are shown to the creator, who can review and report suspected unauthorized AI content.
It follows YouTube's own likeness-detection tool, already expanded to eligible creators and some celebrities.
content_html: If an AI-generated video started circulating with your face on it, would you even know? TikTok is testing a tool meant to answer that. The Verge reports the platform is piloting an opt-in feature, currently limited to a small group of US creators, that scans TikTok for AI-generated content using a creator's likeness and lets them report anything unauthorized.
extra_html: To turn it on, a creator verifies their identity through Jumio — a live selfie plus an ID check. TikTok says it doesn't retain the ID document itself; the facial data collected is used only to match potential likeness hits, which the creator can then review before deciding whether to report a post or account as impersonation. It's a direct response to a problem creators increasingly face: AI tools make it easy to generate convincing video or images of a real, identifiable person without their involvement at all. TikTok isn't first here — YouTube already runs a similar likeness-detection system, which it's expanded beyond ordinary creators to some celebrities and talent agencies. As these tools spread, they're becoming a quiet but important second line of defense alongside platform moderation: not just catching deepfakes after the fact, but giving the person being impersonated a direct way to find and flag them.

related.title: Deepfakes & Misinformation
related.hook: Seeing is no longer believing. AI can now fake a photo, a voice, or a video convincingly enough to fool a quick glance — so the new skill is knowing when to doubt.

related.title: Meta Let You Put Strangers Into AI Photos — Then Pulled It Back Fast
related.hook: Meta's new AI image model could pull any public Instagram user into your AI-generated photos, no permission asked. Backlash was swift, and so was the shutdown.

flashcards.prompt: How does TikTok's new likeness-detection tool work?

choices.text: Creators verify their identity once, then TikTok scans for AI content using their face and flags matches for review
It automatically deletes any video that mentions the creator's name
It blocks all AI-generated content from being uploaded at all

flashcards.explanation_html: After identity verification, the tool scans for potential matches to a creator's likeness, which the creator can then review and report.

flashcards.prompt: What does identity verification for the tool involve, and what does TikTok keep?
flashcards.back_html: A live selfie and ID check via Jumio. TikTok says it does not keep the ID document — facial data is used only to match likeness, not to store your ID.

flashcards.prompt: Is TikTok the first platform to build a tool like this?
flashcards.back_html: No — YouTube already has a similar likeness-detection tool, which it has expanded to eligible creators and even some celebrities and talent agencies.
